name: Rickroll
blurb: A prank link that secretly opens Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up"
title: Rickroll Meme: Meaning, Origin & History
description: A rickroll is a prank link that opens Rick Astley's 1987 hit "Never Gonna Give You Up". It began on 4chan in May 2007 with a fake GTA IV trailer link.
answer: A rickroll is a prank where someone shares a link or video that looks like something interesting but actually plays the music video for Rick Astley's 1987 song "Never Gonna Give You Up". It started on 4chan in May 2007, when a link posing as the new Grand Theft Auto IV trailer led to the song instead. YouTube rickrolled all its users on April Fools' Day 2008, and the original video passed one billion views in July 2021.

body: You click on something promising, a leaked trailer, an answer to your question, an exam result, and instead you see a young Rick Astley in a long coat, dancing a little stiffly and singing "Never gonna give you up, never gonna let you down". Getting tricked is being "rickrolled".
The song itself is a sincere, upbeat 1980s pop hit released on 27 July 1987, which is part of the joke: the surprise is harmless and the tune is very hard to get out of your head.

head: Date
Event
rows: "Never Gonna Give You Up" is released as a single.
On 4chan, the "duckroll" prank (links leading to a picture of a duck on wheels) sets up the bait-and-switch format.
A link posing as the Grand Theft Auto IV trailer leads to the Astley video; it is regarded as the first rickroll.
On 1 April, YouTube makes every featured video on its homepage link to the song.
Astley makes a surprise appearance at the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, singing the song from a float, and wins MTV Europe's "Best Act Ever" award.
The official music video passes one billion views on YouTube.

ul: A shortened or disguised link in a group chat: "exam answers here".
A QR code on a poster or flyer that opens the video.
Typing the lyrics into a conversation, a text version of the prank.
Live rickrolls: a band or crowd suddenly switching into the song at an event.

body: If someone says "never gonna give you up" out of nowhere, you have been rickrolled in text form.

The rickroll is one of the oldest internet pranks that is still in daily use, and it keeps getting new life on every platform. Rick Astley found the attention bizarre at first but came to appreciate it, saying he is grateful that the video and the song took on a life of their own. Because people keep falling for it, the original video keeps climbing in views every year.

faq.a: "Never Gonna Give You Up" by the British singer Rick Astley, released in July 1987.
In May 2007 on 4chan, when a link presented as the Grand Theft Auto IV trailer opened Astley's music video instead.

faq.q: Does Rick Astley mind the meme?
faq.a: Not anymore. He found it strange at first but later said he is grateful for it, and he joined in with a surprise rickroll at the 2008 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
